sources.citation: Endangered Languages Project, 'Wanda' (lang/5076), snapshot 2025-06-09 via the Internet Archive
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on phonology. Resolves 'Mitterhofer 2014' as 'Personal Communication on Wanda' (Bernadette Mitterhofer, SIL, 2014): vitality, location (Kamsamba ward, Momba DC; Kipeta ward, Sumbawanga), orthography 'None'. Quotes Walsh & Swilla 2001: 'Very little has been written about the Wanda people and their language, iciwanda.'

sources.citation: Lindfors, Anna-Lena, Mark Woodward & Louise Nagler. 2009. A sociolinguistic survey of Sichela speech community. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2009-014. Dallas: SIL International. 20 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sichela is treated as a dialect of Wanda (86% probable cognates with the SIL Wanda wordlist, p. 16-17). The wordlist was written 'in broad phonetic transcription using the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA). Tone was not noted.' (p. 9, sec. 3.4). Sec. 3.5 lists only phonological correspondences used for cognate counting (spirantization, metathesis, extra syllables). No word on stress or accent. Cites Daggett et al. 1999 as the only prior document on the Wanda.

sources.citation: Johnston, Harry H. 1919/1922. A Comparative Study of the Bantu and Semi-Bantu Languages, vols. 1-2. Oxford: Clarendon Press.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Wanda appears only as 'ICI-WANDA', a 'northern dialect' of Isi-nyixa (no. 49), vol. 2 p. 60 with footnote 'Quite distinct from the Ici-wandia language (No. 50) farther to the south-east'. No stress remark for Wanda/Nyixa. The footnote 'The accent, it might be mentioned, is always on the penultimate, except where otherwise indicated' (vol. 2, verb paradigmata, p. ~497) is a general note on the sample paradigms (Runyoro etc.), not about Wanda. Vol. 1 has only scattered Ci-wanda vocabulary items.
